targets.query:
import "internal/debug"
import "experimental/record"
import "strings"

selectedRunIds = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "controller_measurement")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.run_id =~ /^${run_id:regex}$/)
  |> keep(columns: ["run_id"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "run_id")
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "run_id"})
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({run_id: r.run_id, run_short: strings.substring(v: r.run_id, start: if strings.strlen(v: r.run_id) > 8 then strings.strlen(v: r.run_id) - 8 else 0, end: strings.strlen(v: r.run_id))}))

runCounts = selectedRunIds

import "internal/debug"
import "experimental/record"
import "strings"

selectedRunIds = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "controller_measurement")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.run_id =~ /^${run_id:regex}$/)
  |> keep(columns: ["run_id"])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "run_id")
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "run_id"})
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({run_id: r.run_id, run_short: strings.substring(v: r.run_id, start: if strings.strlen(v: r.run_id) > 8 then strings.strlen(v: r.run_id) - 8 else 0, end: strings.strlen(v: r.run_id))}))

runCounts = selectedRunIds
  |> group(columns: ["run_short"])
  |> count(column: "run_id")
  |> rename(columns: {run_id: "run_count"})
  |> group()

runLabels = join(tables: {ids: selectedRunIds, counts: runCounts}, on: ["run_short"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({run_id: r.run_id, run_label: if r.run_count > 1 then r.run_id else r.run_short}))
  |> group()

series = from(bucket: v.defaultBucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "controller_measurement")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.run_id =~ /^${run_id:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "tick_seq" or r._field == "elapsed_s" or r._field == "diag_capture_ok" or r._field == "diag_snapshot_stage" or r._field == "diag_refresh_applied" or r._field == "diag_refresh_count")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: string(v: r._value), target: record.get(r: r, key: "target", default: ""), tick_key: record.get(r: r, key: "acceptance_tick", default: "")}))
  |> group()

join(tables: {series: series, labels: runLabels}, on: ["run_id"])
  |> group(columns: ["run_id", "run_label"])
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time", "target", "status", "tick_key"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with tick_seq: if exists r.tick_seq then float(v: r.tick_seq) else debug.null(type: "float")}))
  |> sort(columns: ["_time", "tick_seq", "tick_key"])
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({_time: r._time, run_id: r.run_id, run_label: r.run_label, "Reset": if r.status == "calculated" and exists r.diag_capture_ok and r.diag_capture_ok == "true" and exists r.diag_refresh_applied and r.diag_refresh_applied == "true" and exists r.diag_snapshot_stage and r.diag_snapshot_stage == "refresh_init" and exists r.diag_refresh_count and float(v: r.diag_refresh_count) > 0.0 then 1.0 else debug.null(type: "float")}))

panels.title: Filter Covariance · Reset Level = 1
panels.description: Variance ratio Pii / Pii_initial for the process and growth filters. A reset returns the recorded diagonal ratios to 1, not P to zero; later variance need not decrease monotonically. Orange Reset points mark committed refresh cycles, not input re-anchoring or startup. Check the actual ratios at each marker; a marker alone does not prove reset correctness. Hover for Cycle, Reset Count, raw P and P0 (units shown in their names). G may remain at 1 while paused. Non-positive P or P0 is omitted from the log curves; raw values remain in the tooltip. The dashed Reset Level = 1 reference marks the initial variance. Blank ratio values and Unavailable raw values mean missing, never zero. Full-matrix/off-diagonal correctness and reserve filters require raw records/tests. Native UTC; no averaging or zero filling.

description: Control Targets shows sigma/G target tracking, errors and optimization objectives. Process Measurements & Diagnostics shows temperature, concentration, actual sigma/G, counts, parameters and lag. Both sections collapse independently and share experiment and time filters.
